This PR originally compares character counts between hand written structures in JSON and TOON, but it does not compare actual tool output with token estimation. Here's some testing with large and small tool calls:

```
test/tool/toon-integration.test.ts:
GrepTool - Plain: 48 tokens, TOON: 68 tokens
GlobTool - Plain: 32 tokens, TOON: 48 tokens
Both found 3 files
Large GlobTool - Plain: 1650 tokens, TOON: 1959 tokens
Found 100 TypeScript files
Large GrepTool - Plain: 1441 tokens, TOON: 3337 tokens
Found 100 import matches
Large ListTool - Plain: 552 tokens, TOON: 1565 tokens
Found 100 directory items
```

The grep/glob/list tools did not use JSON structured output, they use a bespoke output format that is specific for the task and more token efficient than any generic structured output could be. I didn't test LSP diagnostics, so TOON may be more efficient than the LSP.Diagnostic.pretty format, possibly if more helpful data was included in LSP diagnostics than there is currently.

I think TOON has great potential to be included in opencode to give tools a choice between string and unknown structured output. This would allow rapid experimentation with custom tools and more maintainable tool implementations in many cases. As for the built-in tools, it's more token efficient to keep using their current output formats, unless more data is added that would scale better with TOON.
